---
title: "Benchmarks against other software"
description: "Peak-area accuracy, spectral ion support and elution-profile recovery across seven workflows on 16 RI-aware simulated GC–MS chromatograms."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

## Sixteen simulated chromatograms

The **16 chromatograms** share a library of **100 reference compounds**.
Each spans a 20-minute retention window, with 1,200 scans and all 258 mass channels.
Compounds are absent from about half the samples, giving **769 true occurrences**.
Library retention indices determine their positions. One compound has a broad
shark-fin-shaped acid profile; the remaining profiles are exponentially modified
Gaussians. Higher concentrations extend peaks towards later times from
approximately fixed leading edges, and a small positive drift shifts successive
injections to the right.

The smooth B-spline background is derived from the experimental `gcmsData2`
window and contributes 3.03% of the integrated compound signal. The simulation
retains its native abundance scale and uses quasi-Poisson noise with
**dispersion 783.18**, estimated from that window. GCMSprime estimates dispersion
separately in each sample, with a **median estimate of 829.55**. The generating
retention-index maps are used for scoring;
the deconvolution receives neither the known areas nor the true profiles.

GCMSprime recovers **734 of 769 occurrences**, with **90 false positives**
(peak F1 **0.922**), including the acid in all seven samples where it occurs.

| Method | Seconds | TP | FP | Sensitivity | Peak F1 | Ion F1 |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GCMSprime | 405.97 | 734 | 90 | 95.4% | 0.922 | 0.938 |
| MS-DIAL | 17.61 | 675 | 641 | 87.8% | 0.647 | 0.858 |
| mzmine GC-EI | 38.47 | 622 | 70 | 80.9% | 0.851 | 0.860 |
| eRah | 17.07 | 645 | 1912 | 83.9% | 0.388 | 0.771 |
| AMDIS | 92.58 | 671 | 1153 | 87.3% | 0.518 | 0.854 |
| xcms + CAMERA | 24.06 | 635 | 146 | 82.6% | 0.819 | 0.617 |
| MSHub | 20.58 | 635 | 2797 | 82.6% | 0.302 | 0.844 |

Times are wall-clock analysis times on an HP ZBook Fury G8 Mobile
Workstation with an Intel Core i9-11950H at 2.60 GHz, eight physical cores
and 16 logical threads, Windows and R 4.5.0. GCMSprime uses 16
single-threaded sample workers, AMDIS runs serially, and xcms + CAMERA uses
four workers. Input conversion is timed separately.

`ncores` can use any number of available cores. GCMSprime parallelizes
deconvolution across sample workers; when enough samples are available,
the independent fitting time can decrease approximately in proportion to
the worker count. The complete analysis also includes coupled refinement
and data transfers.

## Reciprocal spectral matches and integrated areas

The reference library contains all 100 compounds, including those absent
from an individual sample. Candidate spectra must fall within **30 RI units**
and have cosine similarity of at least **0.70**. A reciprocal pair selects
each other as the best eligible spectral hit. Ties are resolved by RI
difference and then ID. A reciprocal hit to a compound actually present is
a true positive; every other returned component is a false positive.
Additional calls to the same reference compound are included in those counts.
Their areas are not added to the selected match.

[![Robust log–log peak-area fits and 95% prediction bands](../reference/figures/simulated-16-area-predictions.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-area-predictions.png)

All panels use **total-ion count equivalents**. Spectra are normalized to
unit L1 norm, with their magnitude transferred to the corresponding profile
or area. Native model-ion areas are corrected for their ion fraction and
integration-time units. The conversions use each engine's exported factors
and acquisition metadata, without calibration against the known answers.
The native values and conversion factors remain in the result objects.

For a component with profile \(h\) and spectrum \(s\), let
\(c=\sum_j s_j\), \(p=s/c\) and \(\widetilde h=ch\).
Then \(hs^\top=\widetilde h p^\top\) and \(\sum_j p_j=1\).
An area measured for a particular ion \(q\) becomes
\(A_{\mathrm{TIC}}=A_q/p_q\), after converting its integration-time units.

The line is a robust log–log fit using `robustbase::lmrob(setting="KS2014")`.
The shaded 95% prediction band uses its robust residual scale and coefficient
covariance, describing the main approximately Gaussian log-error distribution.
Every observed point remains visible, and the dashed **1:1 reference is drawn
last in every panel**. The headings report robust adjusted R²; ordinary
least-squares statistics are retained in the downloadable tables. GCMSprime
has robust adjusted R² **0.996** and a **median absolute area error of 2.01%**.
Area agreement is conditional on recovered true matches, so it is shown
together with sensitivity and false-positive counts.

[![Reciprocal spectral cosine similarity with individual points](../reference/figures/simulated-16-spectral-violin.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-spectral-violin.png)

Each point is a reciprocal spectral hit. Crosses identify hits to compounds
absent from that sample; the cosine axis uses logit spacing. Display values
at or above 0.999999 are shown at 1, while the statistics retain their
original values. Compact horizontal tick labels keep the scale readable.

## Correctness of spectral ion support

[![Within-spectrum ion-support F1 with the shared 0.1% cutoff](../reference/figures/simulated-16-spectral-support.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-spectral-support.png)

Ion support uses a shared **0.1% of base-peak intensity cutoff**, applied
independently to reference and recovered spectra for every method:
\(I_j>0\) and \(I_j\geq0.001\max_l I_l\).
Within-spectrum \(F_1=2TP/(2TP+FP+FN)\) is averaged over correctly matched
true spectra. GCMSprime achieves **mean ion F1 0.938**, compared with
**0.860** for the strongest comparator. Individual points accompany the
violins; the logit-spaced axis retains labels in the original F1 units.

This is also GCMSprime's default spectral reporting cutoff for coefficient
summaries, library queries and MSP/Excel output. `ion_threshold=0` retains
all positive ions. Reporting preserves fitted total ion counts, peak areas,
profiles and information criteria.

## Observed signal and recovered peak areas

[![Observed and true signal with square-root intensity colours](../reference/figures/simulated-16-sample-heatmap.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-sample-heatmap.png)

The observed counts and true mean, including background, use the plotMat
palette with **square-root intensity colours**. Red lines mark true apices.

[![Method-by-compound peak areas with yellow false negatives](../reference/figures/simulated-16-area-heatmap.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-area-heatmap.png)

The ground-truth row and method rows show one sample's true or inferred
total-ion areas. **Bright yellow marks false negatives**; grey marks no signal or
call. Compounds follow increasing RI. A
[pooled view](../reference/figures/simulated-16-area-heatmap-pooled.png)
summarizes all 16 samples; the
[sample-by-sample PDF](../reference/figures/simulated-16-area-heatmaps-all-samples.pdf)
shows every acquisition.

## Correctness of inferred elution profiles

[![Solid inferred and dashed true regular-compound profiles, blue to red by true area](../reference/figures/simulated-16-regular-profiles.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-regular-profiles.png)

[![Solid inferred and dashed true acid-compound profiles, blue to red by true area](../reference/figures/simulated-16-acid-profiles.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-acid-profiles.png)

The first panel set shows the regular compound with the largest total
true area across samples; the second shows the acid compound. All 16 samples
are included and ordered by true abundance, from **blue for the smallest
area to red for the largest**. **Dashed curves are ground truth; solid curves
are returned profiles.** Intensities retain their original total-ion scale,
without unit-area or peak-height normalization. Absent compounds have zero
true signal. Compatible fragments remain separate curves so splitting stays
visible. The generating retention-index calibration supplies the common
horizontal axis; profile amplitudes remain on their native total-ion scale.

GCMSprime recovers these elution profiles most accurately for both the
regular EMG and the shark-fin-shaped acid. Mean profile cosine, counting
missed occurrences as zero, is **0.999 for the regular compound** and
**0.973 for the acid**. Other configurations often truncate profiles,
split their contributions or miss the acid. MS-DIAL also closely recovers
the selected regular compound (mean cosine 0.998). CAMERA supplies a
representative-ion trace scaled to the grouped total-ion area. The mzmine
export here contains spectra and areas without component scan profiles.
MSHub factorizes aligned ion-peak integrals across samples. Its model has
no common compound elution profile constrained to be shared across mass
channels, so component scan profiles are absent from the model itself.
See [Aksenov et al. (2021)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7971188/).

## Detection settings and reproducibility

The xcms + CAMERA configuration uses an **8.6-second filter FWHM**,
signal-to-noise threshold **1.5**, a minimum of **four ions**, and CAMERA
FWHM grouping with `perfwhm=0.8`. Eight alternatives were compared on
odd-numbered samples. The selected setting recovered 321 rather than 301
true occurrences there, while keeping peak F1 within 0.01 of the best
candidate. On the even-numbered samples reserved for checking, recovery
increased from 286 to 314 and F1 from 0.773 to 0.803. Across all samples,
sensitivity increased from **76.3% to 82.6%**. No matching or RI thresholds
were relaxed.

### Recovery across true peak sizes

Sensitivity is also calculated separately in quartiles of true integrated
peak area, including every true occurrence. This makes the preferential
recovery of large peaks visible alongside the conditional area regressions.

| Method | Smallest quarter | Lower-middle | Upper-middle | Largest quarter |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GCMSprime | 91.2% | 95.3% | 96.4% | 99.0% |
| MS-DIAL | 79.3% | 84.4% | 91.1% | 96.4% |
| mzmine GC-EI | 70.5% | 79.2% | 82.3% | 91.7% |
| eRah | 72.0% | 78.6% | 89.1% | 95.8% |
| AMDIS | 78.2% | 83.3% | 89.6% | 97.9% |
| xcms + CAMERA | 66.3% | 81.8% | 84.9% | 97.4% |
| MSHub | 73.6% | 82.8% | 86.5% | 87.5% |

GCMSbenchmark includes the seeded simulation, empirical-background template,
engine settings, scoring tables and plotting code. Its
[installation guide](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/blob/master/GCMSbenchmark/INSTALL.md)
covers the R packages and external engines.

~~~r
library(GCMSbenchmark)
bench <- system.file("benchmarks", package="GCMSbenchmark", mustWork=TRUE)
source(file.path(bench, "simulated-16.R"), encoding="UTF-8")
source(file.path(bench, "plot-simulated-16.R"), encoding="UTF-8")

# Recreate the plots from the included results.
plotBenchmark16(file.path(bench, "results"), "benchmark-figures")

# Generate the same samples and rerun selected installed workflows.
fit <- runBenchmark16("benchmark-run",
  method=c("GCMSprime", "xcms+CAMERA"), ncores=16L)
~~~

The simulation uses seed 9118. The tested versions are MS-DIAL 5.5.261105,
mzmine 4.11.0, eRah 2.2.0, AMDIS 2.71, xcms 4.6.4, CAMERA 1.64.0 and
standalone MSHub revision `59fe5d5d7ad5`. Native engine exports are retained.
The MS-DIAL method and mzmine batch are included. AMDIS uses component
width 16 scans, sensitivity 60, resolution 0 and peak-shape setting 0.

Download the
[summary table](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/blob/master/GCMSbenchmark/inst/benchmarks/results/benchmark.csv),
[matched pairs](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/blob/master/GCMSbenchmark/inst/benchmarks/results/matches.csv),
[all component identifications](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/blob/master/GCMSbenchmark/inst/benchmarks/results/identifications.csv)
and [xcms tuning results](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/blob/master/GCMSbenchmark/inst/benchmarks/results/xcms-training-results.csv).

## Comparison with other software

GCMSprime combines a formally **estimated time-varying point-spread function
(PSF)** with **compound-specific peak shapes**, **grouped peak selection
across mass channels** and a **mathematically specified information
criterion** for automatic compound-count selection.

For its default quasi-Poisson model, the fitted mean and variance satisfy
\(\operatorname{Var}(Y_{it})=\phi\mu_{it}\). The final quasi-GIC combines
the corresponding fit criterion with a penalty for the number of compounds
and their occurrences. Grouped L0 selection uses the mass channels jointly,
and hard log-concavity constrains each component profile. This combination
distinguishes GCMSprime from every evaluated configuration. The other
workflows use peak detection, representative ion traces, correlations,
local covariance, factorization of peak integrals or PARAFAC2 least squares.
Their preprocessing noise estimates and selection rules are summarized below.
[Mathematical basis](algorithm.html)

| Workflow | How it deconvolves and where that can limit recovery | Access |
|:--------|:----------------------------------|:-------------|
| GCMSprime | Estimates a time-varying PSF and uses grouped L0 selection across ions to call peaks. A log-concave factor model fits compound-specific profiles, full spectra and smooth background, with GIC or quasi-GIC selecting the compound count. Samples can share spectra while retaining their own profiles. | Free, GPL open source. [Repository](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime) |
| MS-DIAL | Extracts spectra from detected model peaks within each run, then aligns the features. Smoothing, detection thresholds and the deconvolution window affect which components are recovered. [GC–MS tutorial](https://github.com/systemsomicslab/mtbinfo.github.io/blob/master/MS-DIAL/tutorial.md) | Free, LGPL-3 source. Some vendor readers have separate terms. [MsdialWorkbench](https://github.com/systemsomicslab/MsdialWorkbench#source-code-license) |
| mzmine / ADAP-GC | The benchmark’s GC-EI module groups resolved ions by retention time and shape similarity. Pseudospectra depend on upstream detection, the grouping thresholds and the minimum number of ions. Batch alignment follows extraction. [GC-EI guide](https://mzmine.github.io/mzmine_documentation/latest/module_docs/featdet_spectraldeconvolutiongc/spectraldeconvolutiongc.html) | Free Community licence for eligible academic users. Commercial use requires a paid plan. [Public source](https://github.com/mzmine/mzmine#license) · [Plans](https://mzio.io/plans/) |
| xcms + CAMERA | Detects ion peaks first and then groups them into pseudospectra. Filter widths and grouping rules affect the coverage of weak and coeluting peaks. CAMERA was developed for LC–MS feature annotation. [Kuhl et al. (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1021/ac202450g) | Free, GPL open source. [xcms](https://bioconductor.org/packages/xcms) · [CAMERA](https://bioconductor.org/packages/CAMERA) |
| eRah | Uses local covariance and orthogonal signal deconvolution after filtering and baseline removal. Recovery depends on width and signal thresholds. Cross-sample alignment follows per-sample deconvolution. [eRah manual](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/erah/vignettes/erah-manual.html) | Free, GPL open source. [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=erah) |
| AMDIS | Uses representative ion traces as model peak shapes within each chromatogram. Component width, sensitivity and shape settings govern the calls and extracted spectra. [NIST guide](https://chemdata.nist.gov/mass-spc/amdis/docs/amdis.pdf) | Free standalone binary. [NIST distribution](https://chemdata.nist.gov/dokuwiki/doku.php?id=chemdata%3Aamdis) |
| GNPS/MSHub | Requires a sample series for its NMF workflow. It factorizes aligned peak integrals, so the model resolves spectra and abundances from variation across samples and drops the scan-level profile information. [Aksenov et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3) · [Workflow guide](https://ccms-ucsd.github.io/GNPSDocumentation/gc-ms-deconvolution/) | Free hosted workflow with a GNPS account. Public source under the repository’s nonprofit-use licence. [Source](https://github.com/CCMS-UCSD/GNPS_Workflows/tree/master/mshub-gc) · [Licence](https://github.com/CCMS-UCSD/GNPS_Workflows/blob/733ed89372c3754a4c4d132319da5b4313c47288/LICENSE) |
| PARADISe | Fits PARAFAC2 within retention intervals. Intervals and ranks can require review, and the constant cross-product constraint restricts how peak overlap can change across samples. [Johnsen et al. (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chroma.2017.04.052) · [Protocol](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-2143/v1) | Free Community and paid Professional editions. [Kromath](https://www.kromath.com/) |
